text: When you design a REST API, you need to follow a few simple best practices. First, choose clear and meaningful endpoints, such as /users or /orders, so developers can understand what each one does. Second, always return the correct status codes, like 200 for success, 404 when something is not found, and 500 for server errors. Third, write good documentation that explains every endpoint, its parameters, and its responses. Finally, use versioning to keep your API stable when it changes. For example, you can include the version in the URL, such as /api/v1/users. These practices make your API easier to use, maintain, and update over time.
